statement: DDR4 16GB spot prices reached $81.20, up 17.5% in a month and above the prior peak of $79, while DDR5 16GB broke $50 for the first time after languishing at $39-$41 during the March-to-May correction.
why: Spot memory prices moving to record highs off a spring trough is the fastest visible signal that memory supply is tightening, and it feeds through to the cost of every AI server built.

impact.mechanism: Record spot DRAM prices with a stated month-over-month increase indicate scarce memory supply and rising input cost for accelerator and server builds.

evidence.source: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'"
evidence.excerpt: $81.20 (approximately 116,000 won) as of the previous day, a 17.5% increase from a month earlier

evidence.source: BigGo Finance — "DRAM Spot Prices Hit Record Highs; 'Q3 Contract Prices to Surge Another 25%+'"
evidence.excerpt: breaking through the $50 level (approximately 71,000 won) for the first time ever

confidence.basis: Single secondary finance outlet reporting spot-market quotes; no primary filing and no separately fetched cross-publisher corroboration.

dispersion: DDR4 16GB ranged from about $58 in mid-May to $81.20 now; DDR5 16GB from $39-$41 during the correction to above $50.
